title: The Capxul rebuild
why: The product line drifted from its own description: facts were typed twice and nothing proved the system did what it said.
what: Rebuild on one owner for every fact. The blueprint declares what Capxul does, the world says what runs where, and verdicts made by CI say what is proven.
endState: Capxul's own company runs a month on the rebuilt system in production, with every journey proven by CI and every measure watched.
outOfScope: New product features before the accounts pilot; anything on main or integration/build.

title: Foundations core
goal: One owner for every fact, checked: generated files, the seeded chain, the lint ratchet, machines, the delta check and the blueprint's format.
why: Everything later is declared in the blueprint first, so the blueprint and its checks must exist before any feature is built through it.
doneWhen: Steps 3.5, 3.6 and 3.8 are proven by verdicts on master.

title: The delta check
what: pnpm delta:check fails when an operation lacks a format that exists.
why: New work must be born in the full format, or the ratchets never close.
doneWhen: check:pnpm delta:check runs in the gate on every pull request.

title: The blueprint's format
what: One file per operation, machines import their events, the pipeline's things and the ratchet registry.
why: It is the format every later step writes in.
doneWhen: The people domain moved in full, its journeys green in a fresh world.

title: The glossary
what: Every word for a thing declared once in the blueprint, and the old words counted by a ratchet.
why: Names drift unless one place owns them.
doneWhen: The glossary is generated and ratchet R15 counts the old words.

question: Measure the plumbing now, or after telemetry lands?
problem: The run's plumbing fixes are ready to measure, but telemetry, which would show where the time goes, lands later.
context: A full run takes 27 minutes; the target is 5. Each measured run costs about one dollar of Cloudflare and Neon.

rubric.name: Speed of learning
rubric.why: The sooner we see the gain, the sooner the next fix is chosen.

rubric.name: Cost
rubric.why: The daily cap is ten dollars across all lanes.

options.title: Measure now
options.detail: Run the full journeys tonight without telemetry.
options.tradeoffs: A number tonight, but no breakdown of where the time went.

options.title: Wait for telemetry
options.detail: Measure once telemetry has landed in master.
options.tradeoffs: One complete measurement tomorrow; tonight is lost.

because: The number alone tells us whether the plumbing worked; the breakdown can follow on the next run.

title: Blueprint 2b is in its pull request
parts: Master is green, and the blueprint's stage 2b is in its pull request into master.
It merges once its full run passes. Nothing needs you.

answer.own: Measure now, but run it twice so we see the noise between runs before trusting the number.
